[§ SPO Cheat Sheet §]

[*Scope:*] Quick reminder for the current surface syntax accepted by [.|mTokenizer.] and [.|mSPO_Parser.].
For executable function and module examples, open [<Tests.wiki|Test Examples>].

[=Legend=]
- [.|§.] keyword prefix
- [.|€.] type annotation
- [.|#.] prefix/tag constructor
- [.|=>.] lambda body
- [.|<=>.] generic-lambda marker
- [.|..] method-call statement terminator
- [.|§>.] / [.|§<.] pipe sugar

[=Literals=]
[.spo
|()
|§TRUE
|§FALSE
|123
|-3
|§a
|"abc"
|"
||first line
||second line
|"
|_
.]

[=Data Forms=]
[.spo
|#Box 12
|(a; b)
|(a, b, c)
|{ Name: "Ada", Age: 42 }
.]

[=Patterns=]
[.spo
|x
|§DEF x
|§VAR x
|_
|#Box _
|(a; b)
|(a, b, c)
|{ Name: §DEF name }
|(x & x .> 0)
|(x € MyType)
.]

[=Types=]
[.spo
|[]
|§BOOL
|§INT
|§CHAR
|§TEXT
|§ANY
|§TYPE
|[T; U]
|[T, U, V]
|[#Tag T]
|[§VAR T]
|[T | U | V]
|[Arg => Res]
|[Obj : Arg => Res]
|[§RECURSIVE T Body]
|[§GENERIC T Body]
|[§INTERFACE T Body]
|[.tList §INT]
|[§SIG_WITH t € §TYPE IN Body]
|[§SIG_WITH tF € [§TYPE => §TYPE] IN Body]
.]

[=Commands=]
[.spo
|§DEF Answer = 42
|§DEF Named € §INT = 7
|Pattern = Expression
|
|§VAR x := 1 .
|§VAR y:
|    = 3
|    + 4
|.
|x := 2 .
|
|§RETURN expr
|§RETURN expr IF cond
|
|§RECURSIVE {
|    §DEF Fib = (
|        §DEF n € §INT
|    ) => ...
|}
.]

[=Blocks=]
[.spo
|{
|    §RETURN 1 IF cond
|    §RETURN 0
|}
.]

- blocks are expressions
- there is no implicit "last expression wins"; use [.spo|§RETURN.]

[=Calls Lambdas and Methods=]
[.spo
|2 .+ 5
|3 .<= 5 <= 7
|a .Ord
|
|(x € §INT) => x .* x
|(
|    §DEF t € §TYPE
|) <=> (
|    §DEF x € t
|) => x
|
|§DEF +... = (
|    §VAR X € §INT
|) : (
|    §DEF Y € §INT
|) {
|    X := ((§TO_VAL X) .+ Y).
|}
.]

[=Interfaces=]

An interface object binds a hidden receiver to its methods. The hidden type appears
once, as the first object argument of each method. Other object arguments are allowed.
Calls pass the interface object in that position; the implementation receives the
hidden object. Ordinary arguments and results cannot expose the hidden type.

See [<../SPO_CS/TestFiles/SPO_Functions/10_01_InterfaceObject.SPO|construction, calls and forwarding>],
[<../SPO_CS/TestFiles/SPO_Functions/10_02_InterfaceObjectArguments.SPO|multiple object arguments>] and
[<../SPO_CS/TestFiles/SPO_Functions/10_03_InterfaceMutableObjects.SPO|mutable receivers>].

[.spo
|§DEF iReader = [§INTERFACE t [< Read: [t : [] => §INT] >]]
|§VAR Number := 7 .
|§DEF First = §INTERFACE iReader WITH Number IN {Read: IntRead}
|First : Read => §DEF A .
.]

The method implementation [.|IntRead.] is defined in the linked construction example.
An interface can be assigned to a contract with fewer endpoints when their
signatures are compatible. Consumers typed against the smaller contract continue
to work when the producer adds endpoints. The assignment keeps the same hidden
object and method implementations in a new restricted view. Only the endpoints
in the smaller contract remain available. Assigning that view back to a contract
with additional endpoints is rejected; runtime type matching cannot recover them,
including after transport through [.|§ANY.] or a container. The original wider
interface retains its endpoints.

See [<../SPO_CS/TestFiles/SPO_Functions/10_04_InterfaceNarrowing.SPO|an existing consumer using an extended interface>].
The [<../SPO_CS/TestFiles/SPO_Functions/10_05_InterfaceAuthority.SPO|authority test>]
checks that an omitted admin endpoint cannot be recovered.
Methods are called through the interface object and cannot be extracted as record
fields. The existing mutable-access rules apply: ordinary arguments permit
transport; using mutable state requires an authorized object argument.

[=Modules and Pipes=]
[.spo
|§IMPORT {
|    Std: {
|        ...+...: §DEF ...+... € [[§INT, §INT] => §INT]
|    }
|}
|
|(() .Append 1 §> .Append 2 §> .Append 3)
|.Push 3 To §<.Push 2 To §<.Push 1 To ()
|
|§EXPORT {
|    ...+...: ...+...
|}
|// or: §EXPORT Expression
.]

[=SIG Exports and Imports=]

The [.|Span.] module uses [.spo|§SIG.] to export a range type and its operations:

[#
|../SPO_CS/TestFiles/Modules_SPO/_Modules/Span.SPO
#]

Importing and using the range type:

[| [*Code*] ][ [*Result*] |]
[|
  [#
  |../SPO_CS/TestFiles/Modules_SPO/00_10_SpanConsumer.SPO
  #]
][
  [#
  |../SPO_CS/TestFiles/Modules_SPO/00_10_SpanConsumer.result.SPO
  #]
|]

- [.spo|WITH §DEF F.] binds the imported abstract type as [.spo|F.]
- [.spo|WITH F.] requires another import to use the same type

[=Signature Files=]

A [.|.SIG.] file contains a type definition shared by exports and imports:

[#
|../SPO_CS/TestFiles/Modules_SPO/_Modules/Span.SIG
#]

- use [.spo|[[§LOAD "Span.SIG"]].] in place of a type
- paths are relative to the file containing [.spo|§LOAD.]
- [.|.SIG.] files can load other [.|.SIG.] files

[=Notes=]
- [.spo|§IMPORT.] is a pattern match, not just a name list.
- [.spo|§IS.] is syntax sugar over [.spo|§IF value MATCH { ... }.].
- surface type keywords and IL type keywords differ: [.spo|§RECURSIVE.]/[.spo|§GENERIC.]/[.spo|§INTERFACE.] become [.spo|§REC.]/[.spo|§ALL.]/[.spo|§ANY.] in [.|.ILT.].
